display._about: How changes are shown everywhere: under flat_below (a share, 0.02 = 2%) a change is grey; a comparison with fewer than min_orders orders, or under min_spend rupees of spend, shows n/m instead of a percentage.

meta_view._about: The Meta view's classification, computed once when the pages are built and reused everywhere. SKU: the ordered sku_codes, matched on whole name tokens (names split on _ - | space + and other punctuation except &); a single product also matches with a number or PACK suffix (ITB1, UASPACK). Names are read ad, then ad set, then campaign: the first that names any code wins. A set, kit or range code wins over single products in the same name; two or more single products and no set make one combined row (UAS + ITB) under 'Duos & multi-SKU'. No code: Catalog stage, an offer creative, generic set words, else Other. Offer: 'Offer' (or a price offer like B2@749) in the AD name; Non-offer when the ad, ad set or campaign says Non-offer; anything else is Not tagged so the name can be fixed. Scope: Awareness when the campaign name says awareness, except Reach and Amazon campaigns (sessions.social_name_regex), which are in neither scope.

meta_view.attribution_note: Meta platform data · each ad set's own attribution setting: mostly 7-day click, 1-day view, 1-day engaged-view; a few ad sets use incrementality

watchlist._about: Rule-based flags, at most 6 shown. Spend thresholds are for the picked period.

product_map.sold_in_packs_note: Products sold as Pack of 1 and Pack of 2: the Products tab splits them by pack. The Shopify catalog decides this on every refresh; this list is the backstop when the catalog pull fails (a SKU-less order line on one of these is its pack of 2).
product_map._about: Every Shopify product (keyed on its product ID: titles change) under one house code and short name, used on every tab: rows read 'CODE · Short name'. Packs, sizes and old listings of one product sit under it as variants (the value is the variant's name; empty = the main listing). Freebie, merch, book and gummies products are never counted, so they are not here. A product sold but missing here shows as 'Unmapped' and raises a warning in Data health.

tabs.label: Inventory
tabs.note: Ignored for now: no inventory history source.

flag_spend_without_return._about: Today's campaign tables flag a campaign with at least min_spend rupees spent and no platform value yet, once it is after_hour (IST). Platforms attribute late: a watch flag, not a verdict.

history._about: Today can be compared with any past day (a previous offer, a matching BAU day): hourly Orders, Total sales, sessions and add-to-carts for the last `days` days are kept in cache/live/history.json and published as pages/live_history.json. Missing days are filled `chunk_days` at a time (one Shopify query each for sales and sessions), at most `chunks_per_run` chunks per live run, newest first: 14 x 31 days covers the whole year in the first run. Perf sessions so far are kept for the same number of days.

manual_spends.note: Spends that have no API, read from the team's Google Sheets on every refresh. Sheet ids come from the SPEND_SHEET_* environment variables (see deploy.env.example); the sheets are shared with the dashboard's service account as Viewer.

reddit.label: Reddit
reddit.note: Temporary: the Reddit block of the monthly media-plan workbook (Actual Spend) until the Reddit bot loads BigQuery, all of it performance spend. Up to 31 Oct 2026 the number covers every Reddit campaign, traffic included (the team's rule then); from 1 Nov it is sales campaigns only and traffic spend is awareness. The sheet has no Reddit revenue, so there is no Reddit ROAS.

phase_plan.note: Sale and BAU days from the team's monthly calendar workbooks (the same ones as SPEND_SHEET_REDDIT): the 'Phase' column, else 'Day Type'. Days a workbook covers follow it; other days use the hourly order detection.

manual_spends.estimate_note: Days after a sheet's last filled day, up to estimate_days back from D-1, get an estimated spend (labelled est. on every tab) so Spends and ROAS are not blank while the sheets catch up: affiliate from its recent share of Shopify sales, CRM from a typical recent day of the same kind, Reddit from the day's plan in the media-plan workbook.

live_estimate.note: CRM (flow + broadcast), affiliates and Reddit: today's target spend in the media plan's Target vs Achieved sheet (the same sheet the Target vs achieved table reads) x the share of the day gone. On a day the sheet has no target: affiliates follow sales (their share of GMV on recent same-kind days x today's GMV so far), CRM a typical same-kind day x the share of the day gone, Reddit a typical day since reddit_history_from.

region.note: Region tab: Shopify's Sales report by the shipping address's state and city (and product). City by day is pulled for the whole window every run; product detail one day per query, the last refresh_days again each run and older days backfilled sku_backfill_per_run at a time (app/region.py).

dated_awareness.note: Reddit traffic campaigns are awareness on every day (the team's rule since Nov 2026, applied to the whole history). Set a later 'from' to count them as performance before that date.

reports._about: The Google view's API reports (pipeline additions, docs/google-view-audit.md N1-N10). Each is off until approved. conv_split is on: approved with D1 (conversions = the purchase action only). insights and reach are asked of Google on demand by the view, cached six hours.

commentary.note: The D-1 written commentary is no longer shown (each section now ends with what its table says, and Ask Claude answers questions), so the refresh does not pay for it.

voice.note: Ask Claude's mic: Google Cloud Speech-to-Text in this project (app/voice.py), with the dashboard's vocabulary boosted. Falls back to the browser's own speech recognition if the API is not reachable.

media_plan._about: Target vs achieved: the daily Target Spend and Target GMV of each channel block in the monthly media-plan workbooks ('Target vs Achieved' tab; the same workbooks as SPEND_SHEET_REDDIT). Only targets are read: achieved is the dashboard's own numbers, so it matches every tab. The store row compares Total sales with Performance spend; channel rows compare their performance spend with their platform-attributed revenue (Meta, Google), or the revenue their sheet records (CRM, affiliates). Reddit has no revenue.

google_view._about: Marketing › Google. Tags (computed once in app/google_model.py): scope from the awareness rule; sub_type = taxonomy.google_groups (the Marketing tree's split); segment Brand for brand_sub_types, else Non-brand; campaign_type from Google's channel type (or from the sub_type while the status report is off); SKU from the ad group or asset group name, then the campaign name (the shared meta_view.sku_codes, whole tokens), and per product from the Shopping product report (item shopify_zz_<product id>_<variant id>, mapped through product_map) where that report is on. Conversions and value are the purchase action only (conversion-action category in purchase_categories); other actions (an awareness campaign's add-to-cart) are kept apart. Conversions are by click (interaction) date, data-driven attribution.
google_view.brand_terms_note: Brand terms for the leakage check: the brand name and its misspellings only. Product names (fade forward, even tone underarm mist) are not brand terms (decided 5 Nov 2026).

labels.UNMAPPED: Product not in the product map

targets._about: Platform ROAS / CPA targets per sub_type, unset (null) by default. When set: ROAS green at or above target, amber within target_amber below, red further below; CPA the other way round. Grey under grey_below_cost.

working._about: What's working. Scale: ROAS at or above target (or scale_vs_avg x the segment average when no target) and headroom (Lost IS budget above lost_budget_above, or limited by budget). Fix: cost at or above min_cost and ROAS under fix_below x the target or segment average. Cut: search terms or keywords with cost at or above min_cost and no conversion. Costs are for the picked period.

watchlist._about: Rule-based flags, at most 8 shown; costs are for the picked period.

google_view.attribution_note: Google Ads platform data · conversions = the purchase action only, by click (interaction) date · data-driven attribution

taxonomy._note: How campaign and ad names map to funnel stage, product and Google campaign group. See app/taxonomy.py.

google_groups._about: Offer (price-offer) Performance Max campaigns count as Brand PMax (decided 5 Nov 2026), e.g. WOA_Pmax_Lifetime_Oct_B2@749.

cro._about: The CRO tab (Cooee). Read from Cooee's MCP server by the Cooee sync job (python -m app.cooee.sync) with fixed tool calls; never through a model. Data starts on data_start (Cooee's reports begin there). Each run re-pulls repull_days and back-fills backfill_days_per_run older days. Rows past Cooee's caps are kept as the top `limits` rows per day plus the day totals.

verdict._about: Experiment verdicts, in order: Invalid (split mismatch) when the chi-square test of visitors per arm against the configured split gives p < srm_p; Too early under min_days live or under min_visitors / min_orders in an arm; Winner / Loser when orders per visitor differ with p < alpha; else Inconclusive.

awareness._about: The Awareness tab: is awareness spend growing demand in the geos we spend in, and which geos can we test next? Geo-trackable sales are read from Maplemonk's consolidated sales, read only (sql/awareness/geo_daily.sql); nothing is written to BigQuery. The Awareness job (python -m app.awareness.job) builds the tab's pages and the GeoLift panels in the dashboard's bucket; the GeoLift job (awareness_r/) reads those panels and writes its results back there. Test geos, regions, events and dates all come from here, never from code.
awareness.channels_note: Channels with customer geo. SHOPIFY is never used (an OMS duplicate of WEBSITE). Nykaa, Amazon 1P, B2B and Amazon USA have no customer geo, so every lift is a floor.
